thread:
pavan: heads up — after applying the kernel-selector change on main yesterday we see a regression for TP+PP runs when using INT8 quant. latency jumps ~2x at batch sizes we normally serve (1–4).

eli: can you paste the profiler output / nccl traces?

pavan: here are the top lines from perf run (shortened):
```
SUMMARY: seq=2048 batch=2 tp=2pp=2 int8=true
total_token_time: 1234ms (prev: 610ms)
attention_kernel: fallback to fp32 on shard 1 (selected: aten_cuda_attention_fp32)
allreduce_time: 312ms (was 80ms) // NCCL ring stalls
kv_cache_apply_scale: drift detected: max_abs_diff=7.4e-3 after step 12
kernel_selector: chose generic_matmul_int8 for matmul-3, but slower than expected
```

marta: interesting — two things jump out: 1) kernel selector falling back to fp32 for the attention shard, 2) big all-reduce tail. both could explain 2x latency. the kv drift also hints at scaling mismatch between TP partitions.

sara: is the INT8 scale being broadcast correctly across TP ranks? we had a bug where quant scales were recomputed locally during shard restore.

pavan: good call. i grepped the logs, rank0 has scale=0.127, rank1 has scale=0.129 after warmup. small but enough to corrupt merge and cause more recompute.

eli: that explains attention fallback — numeric instability forced selector to pick fp32 ref kernel. also nccl spike could be due to uneven compute causing long idle in some ranks -> allreduce queueing.

perf-bot: autotune job 1772501001 completed: recommended matmul kernel variant "int8_bf16_tiled_v2" for shape (4096,4096) on A100-40GB.

marta: can we try two quick things in parallel: 1) force consistent scale broadcast before any TP shard step, 2) enable comm/compute overlap (async allreduce) to hide allreduce latency. if perf recovers we know root cause.

pavan: repro steps i used (docker):
```bash
./run_serving_repro.sh --model redwood-3b --tp 2 --pp 2 --quant int8 --batch 2 --seq 2048 --trace nccl,cupti --tune off
```
logs folder: /tmp/repro-1772501234/

eli: i'll spin a canary with forced scale broadcast patch and async allreduce enabled. running now.

(10m later)
eli: canary results — latency back to ~640ms (close to baseline). allreduce_time down to 92ms. attention kernel now uses int8 variant. KV drift eliminated.

marta: excellent. sounds like two contributing factors: local recompute of scale + queuing due to sync allreduce.

pavan: created issue #2345 with repro and attached traces. assigning to @eli for PR that: 1) adds global broadcast of quant scales during shard restore, 2) adds a small timeout + backpressure for allreduce to avoid queue pileups, 3) improves kernel selector logging to show numeric fallbacks.

eli: will open PR in the morning. also adding a unit test that injects per-rank scale divergence and asserts we normalize before attention.

sara: can we add an alert for kv_cache_apply_scale max_abs_diff > 1e-3 in prod? that would catch regressions earlier.

marta: yes. i'll add an observability ticket to link that metric to a pager for dedicated customers.

pavan: thanks everyone. follow-up: if anyone sees similar regressions in other quant modes (fp8) flag it here — might be the same class of bugs.

eli: noted. will include fp8 smoke.

perf-bot: created job 1772501300 to run fp8 smoke + canary for next 6 hours.

marta: closing the thread for now — tracking in #2345. :white_check_mark:
